To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRPC1 receptors are expressed in dendrites of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons and that such expression is co‐localized with metabotropic glutamate 1 (mGlur1) receptors.
TRPC1 protein is mainly localized in dendrites of substantia nigra pars compacta neurons and that TRPC1 and metabotropic glutamatergic receptor 1 are colocalized in dendrites of dopaminergic neurons.

(1) TRPC1 is mainly localized in dendrites of dopamine neurons of the rat substantia nigri; (2) a coexpression of mGluR and TRPC1 was observed in rat substantia nigral dopamine dendrites; (3) TRPC1 immunolabeling was found in the cytosol of glial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of TRCP1 in the rat substantia nigral neurons.
the expression and distribution of TRPC1 at the level of the substantia nigra.
the expression and localization of TRPCs in the substantia nigra, which may provide a new tool to understand the mechanisms underlying dopamine neuron degeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRPC1 receptors are expressed in dendritic processes but not in somata of dopamine neurons of the substantiae nigra.
TRPC1 channels are mainly localized in dendritic processes and to a lesser extent in the soma of dopaminergic neurons, whereas a light TRPC expression has been observed in glial cells.
TRPC1 receptors are expressed in the rat substantia nigral neurons, in particular in their dendrites, and that TRPC1 may play a role in mGlu1‐mediated synaptic plasticity in this brain region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPC1 channels are present in the dendrites of rat SN dopamine neurons, and that their expression is not restricted to the plasma membrane.
TRPC1 channels are localized at the plasma membrane of dendrites of dopamine neurons, where they may be activated in response to mGluR‐mediated glutamatergic inputs.
TRPC1 channels are expressed in the dopaminergic neurons, and that they could be involved in the regulation and modulation of the dopaminergic transmission in the substantia nigrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRPC1 may play a role as a Ca2+ entry pathway in the dendrites of dopamine neurons, thus contributing to their excitability.
TRPC1 may play a role in the modulation of dopamine release in rat substantia nigral neurons.
TRPC1 receptors are expressed in dendritic processes in dopaminergic substantia nigra pars compacta neurons, suggesting a role of TRPC1 channels in the modulation of dopaminergic transmission.
